sentences.text:
For Petitioners : Mr.V.Rajesh Babu
 For Respondents : Mr.V.Vasanthakuma
 Addl. Govt. Plead
 Order

This writ petition has been filed seeking issuance of a writ of mandamus directing second respondent to re-determine the compensation awarded to petitioners' lands acquired at Karasur Revenue Village in Award No.2/2008, based on the application under Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 dated 21.03.2019 and the representation dated 30.05.2024, pursuant to the enhanced compensation award passed in LAOP No.110 of 2012 on the file of II Additional District Judge, Puducherry.
_ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
By consent of learned counsel on both sides, this writ petition is taken up for final disposal at the admission stage itself.

3. The case of the petitioners is that Petitioners' land was acquired for the purpose of setting up of Special Economic Zone by invoking Section 17(4) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, by the first respondent.
Above acquisition was made based on the request of fourth respondent and a notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act came to be published on 24.03.2005.

Acquisition proceeding was completed and since the lands stood in the name of first petitioner's husband, he received a communication dated 04.07.2006 conveying the offer of 80% of compensation in advance.
It is stated that first petitioner's husband produced all relevant documents to prove the ownership and possession.
In the meanwhile, he died leaving behind petitioners as his legal heirs.
The final award came to be passed in Award No.2 of 2008 on 25.01.2008.
Aggrieved by quantum of compensation, one of the land owner preferred an Reference Application seeking enhancement of compensation.
Reference Application _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 04/09/2025 08:44:55 pm ) was taken on file as LAOP.No.110 of 2012.
The said LAOP was disposed of by enhancing the compensation and granting 30% Solatium and 12% Additional Market Value.

Based on the said award in LAOP.No. 110 of 2012,
first petitioner made an application under Section 28(A) of Land Acquisition Act to second respondent seeking to redetermine the compensation awarded to their lands.

Pursuant to the same,
enquiry was conducted on 04.12.2023.

However, the respondents have not come forward to consider the application and therefore, first petitioner submitted a representation dated 30.05.2024 which also remained unanswered and therefore, the petitioners filed the present petition.

However, the process is presently delayed due to non-receipt of requisite funds from the Requisition _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
04/09/2025 08:44:55 pm ) Department and a copy of which has also furnished to petitioners.
The relevant portion of the same is extracted hereunder:

"I am directed to inform that the following petitioners in the writ petition filed vide W.P.No.24558 of 2025 in the High Court of Judicature at Madras for the enhanced compensation u/s.28A of Land Acquisition Act related to the land acquisition for the purpose of "SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONE" in Karasur Revenue Village, Villanur Taluk, Puduchery have already submitted representations for enhanced compensation under Section 28A of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 to our office and they are eligible for the disbursement of enhanced compensation under Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894:
1. Tmt.R.Kowsalya, W/o.Rajulu 2. Tmt.Usha, D/o.Rajulu, W/o.L.Senthilkumar 3. Thiru.R.Balasubramanian, S/o.Rajulu

sentences.text: In this regard, this office has already initiated the necessary action for the sanction and disbursement of the enhanced compensation u/s.28A of Land Acquisition Act, 1984.

However, the process is presently delayed due _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
04/09/2025 08:44:55 pm ) to the non-receipt of requisite funds from the requisition department.
This is for your kind information."

5. Learned counsel for petitioners would only request that the application of petitioners may be considered within a specified time to be fixed by this Court to which learned Additional Government Pleader would submit that they would do so as expeditiously as possible.

6. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case and the stand taken by learned Additional Government Pleader (Puducherry), there shall be a direction to the concerned respondent to consider Section 28(A) application submitted by first petitioner and pass appropriate orders within a period of four months from the date of uploading of the web copy without waiting for the receipt of certified copy.

It is made clear that this Court has not expressed any view with regard to the merits of the case and it is open to the concerned respondent to consider the matter on its own merits and in accordance with law.
_ _ _ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
With the above direction, this Writ Petition is disposed of.
No costs.
